metadata.title: How much dissipation can a multiscale layer cascade carry?
metadata.description:
Multiscale layer constructions produce finite-time blowup for several fluid equations: for the incompressible porous media equation, for the two-dimensional Boussinesq system, for three-dimensional Euler, and, with fractional dissipation |∇|^α of order α < (22 − 8√7)/9, for the forced Navier-Stokes equations. The exponent in the last of these is small, and it is natural to ask what limits it. Exponents in this description are in the |∇|^α convention, in which classical viscosity is α = 2.

We give two upper bounds on the dissipation exponent such constructions can carry. The first is independent of every design constant: a cascade whose layers grow at rate √A on a background gradient A cannot exceed α = 1/2, and one whose layers grow at rate A cannot exceed α = 1. Neither mechanism reaches classical viscosity, by factors of four and two respectively. The second bound applies to the smooth-forcing designs used for the inviscid Boussinesq and Euler results: both are of the pendulum class, and transcribing the exponent content of their force estimates, with the equation and page of every estimate, we show that they certify dissipation only up to α ≤ 5.3×10^−4 (Boussinesq) and α ≤ 6×10^−8 (Euler) at the published choices, and only up to α ≤ 9.0×10^−3 and α ≤ 7.5×10^−3 when every constant of the design is retuned in its favour, at least ten times below the exponent already achieved with a force of finite regularity. In every reading the ceiling is highest when the fewest derivatives of the force are controlled.

Both bounds follow from the amplitude system of the construction together with one additional ingredient, the effect of fractional dissipation on a single layer, which we derive and then test against direct simulation of the nonlinear equations, including the effect of the spatial localization the constructions use. The simulations meet most of their criteria and miss three, which are reported with their numbers: the local growth rate in a two-scale background has a slope 1.36 times the prediction; the handoff from a steered layer to the next reaches a correlation of 0.808 against a criterion of 0.9, and 0.509 at the largest scale separation; and the run at the first chosen parameters grows 726-fold and is refuted by the instability of its own background. We also reconstruct the exponent budget behind the published hypodissipative threshold, identify the constraint that determines it, and show that the admissible frequency ratios form an interval that closes exactly at that threshold, so that cascades with geometrically growing frequencies are excluded at every positive dissipation.

The machine-checked status of the two announced results is reported at the level a kernel replay establishes: the statements and the integrity of the formal proof, not that the formal proof follows the written argument, which Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen (arXiv:2610.08144) report it does not. The mechanism is due to Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa, extended to smooth forcing by Alpogé and Buckmaster; nothing here establishes blowup for any equation or improves any published threshold.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/analysis-pde/navier-stokes).
metadata.version_notes: Failed criteria are now reported: the slope of the two-scale handoff test is 1.36 times the prediction (criterion not met); the steered two-layer handoff reaches a correlation of 0.808 against a criterion of 0.9, and 0.509 at the largest separation (criterion not met; the base-only control discriminates in three of five runs); the steered cycle at the first chosen parameters is refuted (726-fold growth, Rayleigh-Taylor instability of the background); the dynamical handoff without steering is inconclusive. The verification section is now a table of every criterion with its numbers and what follows from it. The transcribed design bounds are checkable: the equation and page of every estimate of the two Alpogé-Buckmaster papers, their identifiers and hashes, the thirteen Euler coefficient quotients, and the displayed inequalities and arithmetic behind case (iii) of both theorems (4.48e-3 and 3.77e-3). A numerical-methods section gives grids, integrator, steps, domain, parameters, hardware, run times, code paths and commands, and the data section points to the repository test that guards the quoted numbers. Evidence marks [V], [D], [MV], [U], [C] are added throughout. Conventions are stated at every number: 3.12e-3 is in our convention (6.25e-3 in the |∇|^α convention), 0.0350 is in the |∇|^α convention, and the abstract names its convention. The measured agreement of the peak growth rate is 8.6e-5 at phi = pi/2 and 4.1e-5 at phi = pi/4 (the earlier text gave 4e-5 for both). The identity for the fractional Laplacian is stated for a single mode and its use for a multi-harmonic profile is marked as a conjecture; Theorem 3.1 gains the hypothesis that the background gradients are unbounded, with a remark on a stage-dependent frequency exponent. The status section reports the repository, toolchain, job counts, axiom lists and kernel replay times. The bibliography is corrected (titles of the Cordoba-Lain-Sanclemente-Martinez-Zoroa Boussinesq paper, of the Alpogé-Buckmaster-Coiculescu porous-media paper with its third author, and of the two OpenAI manuscripts) and gains URLs. Three figures are added from the result files.
